GENERAL SCIENCE — TERMLY EXAM #7
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: GENERAL SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Polymers? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Polymers.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Polymers.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Polymers.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Polymers.

2. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 37 °C

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Electrostatics 3.2 Current Electricity 3.3 Mains Electricity 3.4 Projectile Moti? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Electrostatics 3.2 Current Electricity 3.3 Mains Electricity 3.4 Projectile Moti.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Electrostatics 3.2 Current Electricity 3.3 Mains Electricity 3.4 Projectile Moti.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Electrostatics 3.2 Current Electricity 3.3 Mains Electricity 3.4 Projectile Moti.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electrostatics 3.2 Current Electricity 3.3 Mains Electricity 3.4 Projectile Moti.

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Ecosystems? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Ecosystems.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Ecosystems.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on The Ecosystems.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Ecosystems.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Detergents ● Soapy and soapless detergents ● Preparations of detergents ● Mode o? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Detergents ● Soapy and soapless detergents ● Preparations of detergents ● Mode o.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Detergents ● Soapy and soapless detergents ● Preparations of detergents ● Mode o.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Detergents ● Soapy and soapless detergents ● Preparations of detergents ● Mode o.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Detergents ● Soapy and soapless detergents ● Preparations of detergents ● Mode o.

6. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cell division? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cell division.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cell division.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Cell division.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cell division.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Carbon and its Oxides? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Carbon and its Oxides.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Carbon and its Oxides.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Carbon and its Oxides.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Carbon and its Oxides.

9. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Ice melting to water

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Evolution and Biodiversity? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Evolution and Biodiversity.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Evolution and Biodiversity.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Evolution and Biodiversity.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Evolution and Biodiversity.

11. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Producers
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Primary consumers only

12. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. watt (W)
   D. newton (N)

13. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Electrolysis? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Electrolysis.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electrolysis.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Electrolysis.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Electrolysis.

15. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any substance that conducts electricity
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

16. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Removing all vegetation

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Skeletal and Muscular System and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Carbon and its Oxides and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Alkanols, Alkanoic Acids and Esters. and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Detergents ● Soapy and soapless detergents ● Preparations of detergents ● Mode o and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Polymers and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Electrolysis and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
